newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude turns higher as lower temps forecast.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude turns higher as lower temps forecast.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil and prodcuts futures ended higher Wednesday, reversing initial losses on higher inventory figures after forecasts for U.S. weather changed to below-normal temperatures extending into next week.

February crude ended 37 cents higher at $26.60 a barrel, having earlier hit a low of $25.85. Heating oil futures led the market, with February bouncing from a low of 71.50 cents a gallon to end up 0.71 cents at 73.20 cents.
"A lot of people discounted the builds in products stocks on the colder weather," said Thomas Blakeslee, a trader at Cargill Investor Services.
"Also, it is really just a very resiliant market," Blakeslee added. "There was not only some short-covering but new buying."
Traders had expected the pressure on the "crack spreads" which began on Tuesday to continue this session following bearish stocks data.
The Energy Information Agency (EIA) Wednesday reported even larger builds than the American Petroleum Institute (API) on Tuesday, which were above what market participants were forecasting.

The EIA reported a build of 6.2 million barrels in gasoline stocks last week, higher than the 4.25 million-barrel build recorded by the API. EIA distillate stocks rose 3.1 million barrels, compared with 2.9 million increase in the API report and more than double 1.5 million barrels forecast by the market participants surveyed by Reuters on Tuesday.
A sharp decline in imports of crude saw the API and EIA report a decline in stocks last week of 9.5 and and 8.5 million-barrel decline, respectively.
However, analysts noted that the crude stocks decline could be explained by some end-year tax avoiding as well as the closure of the Houston ship channel last week for bad weather.

"Remaining concern about cold weather headed for the northeast come the weekend seems like the logical reason (for heating oil leading the market higher) but we're still a bit puzzled," said Tim Evans, an analyst at Pegasus Econometrics, in an afternoon report.

"Crude oil was in stronger shape technically and it certainly had the more bullish inventory data. Perhaps this is an indication that heating oil is coming back into favor with speculators," Evans added.
Gasoline trailed behind and February gained only 0.09 cents to end at 72.19 cents a gallon, having traded a 70.70/72.40 cents range.
